humanities_role_explanation: Historical newspaper text (BLN600) supplies the data, but the competence tested is generic post-OCR error correction measured by character error rate; no historical, philological or interpretive competence is assessed.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Text-only: noisy OCR text strings are input and corrected text is output. Source page images are not given to the models.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Post-OCR correction framed as sequence-to-sequence translation or prompt-based correction ('Fix the OCR errors in the provided text'). Error types discussed: substitution, insertion, deletion, misnamed entities, hallucination.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Single-task study (post-OCR correction) on one corpus; it does not introduce a benchmark.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: Llama 2 7B and 13B base models with LoRA instruction-tuning, compared with fine-tuned BART base and large.

quantitative_metrics.note: Percentage reduction in character error rate (CER).

summary: The paper instruction-tunes Llama 2 (7B, 13B) with LoRA for post-OCR correction of BLN600, a corpus of 19th-century British newspaper articles, and compares it with fine-tuned BART. Llama 2 13B reduces CER by 54.51% against 23.30% for BART large, and Llama 2 also performs well with little training data.
key_findings: Llama 2 13B achieves a 54.51% CER reduction, Llama 2 7B 43.26%, BART large 23.30% and BART base 14.60%. Llama 2 does well from the smallest training subset (80 samples), while BART improves substantially with more data. Substitutions and deletions are easiest to correct; insertions and heavily corrupted entity names are hardest.
facets_explanation: Reference texts are the manually re-keyed human transcriptions in BLN600, made from the source images and produced before this paper as part of the corpus. The paper does not discuss annotator disagreement or alternative valid corrections. Correction is scored against a single reference by CER.
results_explanation: Table 3 reports 'Llama 2 13B 54.51' as CER Reduction (%), the mean over five training and evaluation iterations; BART 400M reaches 23.30. The metric is percentage reduction in CER, not a standard listed metric, so it is recorded as other. No human baseline is reported. The paper evaluates a single format and reports no cross-cultural comparison.

humanities_role.quote: Poor OCR quality continues to be a major obstacle for humanities scholars seeking to make use of digitised primary sources such as historical newspapers.

dataset_size.quote: Comprising 600 samples, the articles are sourced from six different publications

primary_evaluation_setting.quote: By instruction-tuning Llama 2 and comparing it to a fine-tuned BART on BLN600

gold_source.quote: along with high-quality manually re-keyed human transcriptions from the source images

gold_beyond_stimulus.quote: For each ground truth segment, the corresponding OCR text is then gathered using a search algorithm

answer_multiplicity.quote: computing the Levenshtein distance between the recognised text and the reference text
